title: Repo market networks: dynamics under financial stress
summary: This ECB Working Paper examines the resilience of the euro-denominated repo market during episodes of financial stress using transaction-level data and network analysis from 2021 to mid-February 2025. The paper finds that the institutional repo network exhibits a core-periphery structure where connectivity intensifies during stress periods, with connections between banks growing even during stress. At the sectoral level, trading volumes and repo spreads remain broadly stable, and at the market level, borrowing costs decline as financial stress increases, indicating the euro repo market functions as a shock absorber.
key_points: Euro repo market has core-periphery network structure with small core of highly active institutions conducting most trading
Connections between institutions, especially bank-to-bank trading, have grown over time even during stress periods
Financial stress is associated with lower spreads at market level, consistent with repo market functioning as a shock absorber
Trading volumes and borrowing costs between different institution types remain stable under stress
Repo market is largest segment of euro money market: 56% of daily transactions, 30% of outstanding amounts
Total outstanding repos increased 4.9% from June 2023 to June 2024 according to ICMA survey of 61 European financial institutions
NBFIs play increasingly prominent role in repo markets, with potential for vulnerabilities to propagate more rapidly
why_it_matters: This research provides empirical evidence on how the euro repo market—the largest segment of euro money markets—behaves under financial stress. Understanding that repo spreads decline during stress periods (shock absorber function) contradicts assumptions that stress always tightens liquidity conditions. The core-periphery structure finding has implications for systemic risk monitoring: stress events may concentrate in a small group of highly connected institutions. Regulators and financial institutions can use these insights to design more resilient market structures and better anticipate contagion risks.
market_structure_context: The paper directly analyzes repo market network topology, finding a core-periphery structure with intensified connectivity during stress. It examines density and strength metrics, repo spreads, haircuts, and maturities across stress periods. The analysis reveals that bank-to-bank connections have grown over time, and that the repo market maintains stable trading volumes and declining spreads during stress—indicating resilient market plumbing that absorbs shocks through pricing adjustments rather than volume disruptions.
important_numbers: 56% of daily euro money market transactions
4.9% increase in outstanding repos (June 2023 to June 2024)
